key_insight: Axion makes differentiable phase-field fracture simulation GPU-native by compiling the full finite element solution workflow into a single JAX program.
engineering_relevance: It accelerates computationally demanding fracture analyses while enabling solution sensitivities to material and model parameters.
method: JIT-compile element kernels, nonlinear solvers, damage constraints, and load stepping for GPU execution without host intervention.
Use forward-mode automatic differentiation for consistent tangents and differentiate the solver program for parameter sensitivities.
Apply global operators matrix-free, with fixed-array octree refinement and multi-GPU domain decomposition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 37.9× speedup over single-CPU FEniCSx at identical 2D discretization, 92% strong and 96% weak scaling efficiency on four GPUs, and a 96M-DOF dam demonstration on one GPU.
watch_item: The reported speedup compares different hardware platforms, so it should not be interpreted as a hardware-independent algorithmic advantage.
paper_title: Axion: A differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework,demonstrated on phase-field fracture
